abstract:
Neutrinos are the lightest known matter particles, far lighter than any of their relatives. [[t]] This trail follows how the framework accounts for them, one step at a time. [[t]]

It finds a right-handed neutrino, which the Standard Model treats as optional, with its zero hypercharge fixed by the framework's own construction. [[c:neutrino.empty-twistor]] Assuming a large Majorana mass (Premise (M)), the seesaw makes the light masses small, and because the family couplings start out evenly weighted, only one light neutrino gets a mass at first approximation. [[c:neutrino.rank-one-seesaw-ordering-sum-double]]

If the second stage of symmetry breaking is hierarchical (Premise (H)), the three masses add up to about 0.059 eV, the smallest total oscillation experiments allow. [[c:pred.neutrino-mass-sum-floor]] The walk ends with the matter-antimatter imbalance and with predictions that running experiments can test. [[t]]
introduction:
The walk starts with the particle that makes the seesaw possible, sets aside one idea that failed, and then builds the seesaw piece by piece. [[t]]

It closes with the predictions the seesaw makes and what they say about the early universe. [[t]]
i:neutrinos: Each step below adds one piece to the account of why neutrinos are so light. [[t]]
t:^>neutrino.empty-twistor:
The story starts with a right-handed neutrino, a particle the Standard Model treats as optional. [[c:neutrino.empty-twistor]] In this framework it is not optional: it is the empty conformal spinor, the state of one conformal spinor with no pair mode occupied. [[c:neutrino.empty-twistor]]

Its hypercharge is zero, and that value comes from the framework's own construction, since anomaly cancellation alone would have left it free. [[c:neutrino.empty-twistor]]
t:neutrino.empty-twistor>refuted.the-neu:
With a partner for the neutrino in hand, the next question is what sets the neutrino's mass. [[t]] One early idea was that the cosmological term of the deformed bracket could do it. [[c:refuted.the-neutrino-mass-is-set-by-the-cosmological-ter]]

That term lies below the flat term by the factor $\Lambda l^{2}/6$ for a composite of extent $l$, so it never dominates for anything smaller than the horizon. [[c:neutrino.seesaw-what-gauge-invariance-proves-what]] The idea is refuted and kept on the record. [[c:refuted.the-neutrino-mass-is-set-by-the-cosmological-ter]]
t:refuted.the-neutrino-mass-is-set-by-th:
What remains is the familiar seesaw, and this step separates what in it is proved from what is assumed. [[t]] Gauge invariance allows exactly one fermion mass that needs no condensate: a Majorana mass for the right-handed neutrino. [[c:neutrino.seesaw-what-gauge-invariance-proves-what]]

Assuming, as Premise (M), that the framework realises that mass at a large scale $M_{R}$, the leading-order seesaw for one generation gives \[ m_{\nu} = \frac{m_{D}^{2}}{M_{R}}, \] with $m_{D}$ the ordinary Dirac mass, which is why the light mass comes out so small. [[c:neutrino.seesaw-what-gauge-invariance-proves-what]]
t:neutrino.seesaw-what-gauge-invariance-:
The seesaw needs the pattern of neutrino couplings across the three families, so the trail pauses for a piece of pure algebra. [[t]]

A real symmetric $3 \times 3$ matrix that is unchanged when the families are permuted has only two free numbers: \[ S = \alpha\mathbf{1} + \beta\J, \] with $\J$ the all-ones matrix. [[c:neutrino.invariant-symmetric-matrices]] It has eigenvalue $\alpha + 3\beta$ on the democratic direction $u' = (1,1,1)$ and $\alpha$ on the plane orthogonal to it, which makes it easy to invert. [[c:neutrino.invariant-symmetric-matrices]]
t:neutrino.invariant-symmetric-matrices>:
Now the pieces combine. [[t]] The Dirac couplings treat the three families identically at leading order, so the Dirac mass matrix is \[ \mD = d\,\J, \] with the single Dirac eigenvalue $m_{D} = 3d$ along $u'$. [[c:neutrino.rank-one-seesaw-ordering-sum-double]]

Under Premise (M) only one light neutrino then gets a mass through the seesaw, and the ordering is normal. [[c:neutrino.rank-one-seesaw-ordering-sum-double]] If the second stage of the breaking is hierarchical (Premise (H)), the sum sits at the oscillation floor. [[c:neutrino.rank-one-seesaw-ordering-sum-double]]
t:neutrino.rank-one-seesaw-ordering-sum-:
At first approximation only one light neutrino has a mass, so the next step asks how a second one gets its mass. [[c:neutrino.rank-one-seesaw-ordering-sum-double]]

A Dirac breaking of size $\delta$, written $\mD = d(\J + \delta A)$, lifts the second light mass at order $\delta^{2}M_{3}/\alpha$, with $\alpha$ and $M_{3}$ the two heavy scales. [[c:neutrino.breaking-relation]] A breaking of the Majorana sector alone lifts nothing. [[c:neutrino.breaking-relation]]
t:neutrino.breaking-relation>pred.neutri:
This sets up the first prediction that a measurement can check. [[t]]

Under Premise (H) the neutrino mass sum lies at the normal-ordering floor, \[ \mnu \approx 0.059 \text{ eV} \] [[c:pred.neutrino-mass-sum-floor]] Cosmological surveys are now close to this value, so it is a near-term test. [[c:pred.neutrino-mass-sum-floor]]
t:pred.neutrino-mass-sum-floor>pred.no-n:
The same premise bears on neutrinoless double-beta decay, a rare nuclear process that would show neutrinos are their own antiparticles. [[c:pred.no-neutrinoless-double-beta]]

Under Premise (H) the effective mass $m_{\beta\beta}$ that sets its rate lies in the hull from $1.3$ to $3.9$ meV, below next-generation sensitivity. [[c:pred.no-neutrinoless-double-beta]] A clear signal there would count against the framework, so the predicted absence is itself a test. [[c:pred.no-neutrinoless-double-beta]]
t:pred.no-neutrinoless-double-beta>neutr:
Heavy neutrinos are also the textbook mechanism of leptogenesis, the standard account of why the universe holds more matter than antimatter. [[c:neutrino.leptogenesis-suppressed-alignment-reheating-premise-new]]

Here that mechanism must not operate, and it is suppressed in three steps: by the democratic alignment at leading order, by Premise (R) against washout and the resonant pair, and by real breaking for the phases. [[c:neutrino.leptogenesis-suppressed-alignment-reheating-premise-new]] Premise (R) is an assumption: that the descent reheats below the lower heavy scale, so no heavy neutrino ever thermalised. [[c:neutrino.r-descent-reheats-below-lower-heavy]]
t:neutrino.leptogenesis-suppressed-align:
The leptogenesis result ends in a stance that experiment can test. [[t]]

Under the real-breaking assumption the Dirac CP phase of lepton mixing is trivial, \[ \delta_{CP} \in \{0, \pi\} \] [[c:pred.leptonic-cp-trivial]] A measured CP phase away from these two values would refute it. [[c:pred.leptonic-cp-trivial]]
conclusion:
Taken together, the seesaw with democratic Dirac couplings gives one light neutrino its mass first, fixes a normal ordering, and puts the sum at the oscillation floor under Premise (H). [[c:neutrino.rank-one-seesaw-ordering-sum-double]]

The trail rests on stated assumptions: that the framework realises a large Majorana mass (Premise (M)), that the second stage of breaking is hierarchical (Premise (H)), that the early universe never reheated enough to make heavy neutrinos (Premise (R)), and that the rank-one eigenvalues coincide at the ceiling (Hypothesis (U)). [[t]] A mass sum away from the floor, a double-beta signal, or a nontrivial leptonic CP phase would each count against the picture. [[t]]
